metadata.title: Snyk: developer-first SCA/SAST/container/IaC on the software supply chain

entities.name: Snyk
entities.notes: Developer security platform: Snyk Open Source (SCA), Snyk Code (SAST), Snyk Container, Snyk IaC, plus secrets and (2026) agentic/AI-code validation. Sits in the IDE/CLI/PR, not in the SOC. Distinct from Huntress (MDR) and CrowdStrike (endpoint EDR). Founded on open-source vulnerability intel; Trust Center lists ISO 27001 / SOC2. Customer-code-not-used-for-training is a vendor policy claim.

entities.name: SCA
entities.notes: Software composition analysis: known vulns and licenses in third-party packages. Why it works: most app risk is transitive deps, not first-party logic, and SCA is the control that sees the SBOM. Failure: 0-days not yet in the intel DB; unreachable CVEs as noise; does not stop a malicious maintainer who ships a clean version then a bad one (xz-utils / npm worm class) until the signature is published.

entities.name: SAST
entities.notes: Static application security testing of first-party code (Snyk Code). Why it works: finds injection/authz classes before runtime. Failure: logic bugs, business-rule IDOR, and generated-code volume that outruns review.

entities.name: npm_Ecosystem
entities.notes: JavaScript package registry. Recurring supply-chain target (typosquats, maintainer-account takeover, worms). Snyk's Trust Center (Aug 2026) documents Snyk identifying an active npm supply-chain campaign (Keyv/Cacheable 'ChainDrop') affecting hundreds of packages - Snyk as observer/defender of the ecosystem, not asserted as the initial victim.

edges.instrument: detects known-bad packages after intel lands; does not prevent first-day maintainer compromise
SCA + published intel; Aug 2026 ChainDrop identification (Trust Center)
SCA findings feed the n-day fix queue (app deps, not OS KEV)
peer protectors, different plane: AppSec/SCA vs MDR/SOC
peer market (developer platform vs endpoint EDR)
signed update as the route SCA does not see (build system, not a CVE in a dep)
edges.notes: SCA would not have stopped SolarWinds; that is a signed-build compromise, not a vulnerable library version.
